decisions.reason: After dropping the parallel unit B, A remains the firm's only two-component injection option, and four years on it serves a niche the firm knows well at low holding cost, so the option is still worth keeping, though uncertainty about its value is largely resolved and no strong signal supports a bigger commitment.
The automatic airless gun shares components with the core pump range and costs little to keep, so there is no evidence justifying abandonment.
A manual airless gun is a staple that complements the pump business at minimal holding cost, so it stays on the market.
The air-assisted multi-model line is now mature enough to prune weak variants, but the line as a whole fits the core spray business and is cheap to hold, so it is kept.
